[EFFECT]
Clear weather (category 1) gives a small positive boost to predicted demand (around +0.05 in log space), while misty or cloudy conditions (category 2) have virtually no effect. Once precipitation arrives — light rain or snow (category 3) — demand drops sharply by about −0.35 in log space, the largest penalty of all four categories. Interestingly, heavy rain (category 4) is slightly less penalising (~−0.26) than light rain/snow, though both substantially reduce ridership compared to dry conditions.

[IMPORTANCE]
With an importance score of 0.061 and a rank of 6 out of 9 features, weather situation has a moderate influence on predicted demand — meaningful but less decisive than the top features such as hour of the day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan for noticeably lower bike availability needs and reduced staffing during rainy or snowy hours, as precipitation cuts predicted demand by roughly 25–30%; conversely, ensure full bike availability during clear-weather periods when demand is at its highest.
